model_numbers: XT2309-2 (global); BR retail via Motorola/Lenovo B2B channel
notes: B2B-focused flagship. Brazil launch Mar 2023 at R$5,499 official (Lenovo/Motorola corporate channels, also sold at retail; cash price R$4,839.99 at launch). NOT officially launched in India — Amazon.in/aggregator listings (~Rs 35,999) are grey imports. Android 16 OTA confirmed shipping (build W1U136H.39-17, rollout reported Mar 2026) — input's Android-15 ceiling corrected; 16 is the final major version. Largely discontinued.
caveats: Advertised 120° UW (GSMArena-confirmed) is a comfortable FOV pass on paper, BUT Motorola HALs are historically mixed on exposing the ultrawide to third-party Camera2 apps (GameChanger: UW IDs hidden despite native-app access; some Edge-era models report third-party success — Lenovo forum Edge 30 Ultra thread). GCam-port sites claim 0.6x UW switching works on ThinkPhone, but that evidence is templated/low-trust and does not confirm the app's specific CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO-below-1.0 mechanism vs a separate camera ID — runtime compat-probe must decide. Encoder: Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 (c2.qti.hevc.encoder) is in the known-reliable Qualcomm 8-series bucket (documented CBR support, timestamp-honoring rate control, no B-frame insertion reports). ARCore-certified (codename bronco appears in the ARCore device list) — strong proxy for sustained ≥100 Hz IMU and REALTIME camera timestamp source, but not in-house measured. Thermal: SD 8+ Gen 1 runs notably cooler than 8 Gen 1 and 1080p30 HEVC is light load; 25-min sustained capture not directly tested. Logistics: Brazil-only official availability (B2B-focused channel), no official India sale, and the device is largely discontinued — fleet acquisition may be hard. Android 16 is the last major OS version.
